results.name: session_midsession_plateau
results.description: Yes-rate on trials 100-274 minus the average of the yes-rates on trials 0-99 and 275-449; observed > null means the relaxation of the yes criterion happens early then plateaus (concave), which the model linear-in-trial criterion drift cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: session_midsession_plateau
# description: Yes-rate on trials 100-274 minus the average of the yes-rates on trials 0-99 and 275-449; observed > null means the relaxation of the yes criterion happens early then plateaus (concave), which the model linear-in-trial criterion drift cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    return m((ti >= 100) & (ti < 275)) - 0.5 * (m(ti < 100) + m(ti >= 275))

results.name: log_magnitude_region_gap
results.description: Among out-of-span targets with gap 5-40 from the span, yes-rate when the nearest bounding example is <=20 minus when it is >=60; observed < null means equal linear gaps hurt more among small numbers (log-like compression), which the model under-produces.
results.code:
# name: log_magnitude_region_gap
# description: Among out-of-span targets with gap 5-40 from the span, yes-rate when the nearest bounding example is <=20 minus when it is >=60; observed < null means equal linear gaps hurt more among small numbers (log-like compression), which the model under-produces.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    sel = (gap >= 5) & (gap <= 40)
    bound = np.where(t < mn, mn, mx)
    return m(sel & (bound <= 20)) - m(sel & (bound >= 60))

results.name: below_vs_above_span_asymmetry
results.description: Yes-rate for targets 5-40 below the smallest example minus targets 5-40 above the largest example; observed < null means people generalize less downward than upward (log-like magnitude: equal linear gaps below are larger ratios), which the symmetric linear-distance model fails to produce.
results.code:
# name: below_vs_above_span_asymmetry
# description: Yes-rate for targets 5-40 below the smallest example minus targets 5-40 above the largest example; observed < null means people generalize less downward than upward (log-like magnitude: equal linear gaps below are larger ratios), which the symmetric linear-distance model fails to produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    return m((mn - t >= 5) & (mn - t <= 40)) - m((t - mx >= 5) & (t - mx <= 40))

results.name: drift_by_distance_interaction
results.description: Late-minus-early (trial_index >=225 vs <225) yes-rate change among far targets (gap >30 outside span) minus the same change among in-span non-example targets; observed > null means the session-long relaxation of criterion concentrates on far/unlikely targets (broadening generalization) more than the model additive logit drift predicts.
results.code:
# name: drift_by_distance_interaction
# description: Late-minus-early (trial_index >=225 vs <225) yes-rate change among far targets (gap >30 outside span) minus the same change among in-span non-example targets; observed > null means the session-long relaxation of criterion concentrates on far/unlikely targets (broadening generalization) more than the model additive logit drift predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    late = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy() >= 225
    far = gap > 30
    near = (gap == 0) & ~isex & (k >= 2)
    return (m(far & late) - m(far & ~late)) - (m(near & late) - m(near & ~late))

results.name: round_number_target_contrast
results.description: For sets with no multiple-of-10 example, among out-of-span targets, yes-rate on multiples of 10 minus other targets; observed > null means people are attracted to round numbers beyond what final-digit similarity predicts, observed < null means they avoid them more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: round_number_target_contrast
# description: For sets with no multiple-of-10 example, among out-of-span targets, yes-rate on multiples of 10 minus other targets; observed > null means people are attracted to round numbers beyond what final-digit similarity predicts, observed < null means they avoid them more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    has10 = (ex.to_numpy() % 10 == 0).any(axis=1)
    sel = ~has10 & (gap > 0)
    return m(sel & (t % 10 == 0)) - m(sel & (t % 10 != 0))

results.name: exact_boost_by_set_size
results.description: Exact-example boost (yes-rate on target = an example minus yes-rate on non-example targets within 1-3 of the nearest example) for 4-example sets minus the same boost for 1-3-example sets; observed < null means the fixed-list concept is less credible for larger sets than the model constant list weight implies.
results.code:
# name: exact_boost_by_set_size
# description: Exact-example boost (yes-rate on target = an example minus yes-rate on non-example targets within 1-3 of the nearest example) for 4-example sets minus the same boost for 1-3-example sets; observed < null means the fixed-list concept is less credible for larger sets than the model constant list weight implies.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    near = ~isex & (nearest >= 1) & (nearest <= 3)
    b4 = m(isex & (k == 4)) - m(near & (k == 4))
    bs = m(isex & (k <= 3)) - m(near & (k <= 3))
    return b4 - bs

results.name: interior_span_width_contrast
results.description: Yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the span of 2+ examples when the span is >=50 minus when it is <=25; observed > null means people fill in wide spans more readily than the model (which treats all interior targets as zero size-mismatch), observed < null means less readily.
results.code:
# name: interior_span_width_contrast
# description: Yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the span of 2+ examples when the span is >=50 minus when it is <=25; observed > null means people fill in wide spans more readily than the model (which treats all interior targets as zero size-mismatch), observed < null means less readily.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    sel = (k >= 2) & (gap == 0) & ~isex
    span = mx - mn
    return m(sel & (span >= 50)) - m(sel & (span <= 25))

results.name: first_vs_last_exact_example
results.description: In sets of 2+ examples, yes-rate when the target is the first-shown example minus when it is the last-shown example; observed > null means people show primacy for repeated examples, whereas the model's recency-weighted memory predicts the last example is endorsed more.
results.code:
# name: first_vs_last_exact_example
# description: In sets of 2+ examples, yes-rate when the target is the first-shown example minus when it is the last-shown example; observed > null means people show primacy for repeated examples, whereas the model's recency-weighted memory predicts the last example is endorsed more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = ex.min(axis=1).to_numpy(); mx = ex.max(axis=1).to_numpy()
    k = ex.notna().sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
    first = ex[0].to_numpy(); last = ex.ffill(axis=1).iloc[:, -1].to_numpy()
    isex = ex.eq(pd.Series(t, index=ex.index), axis=0).any(axis=1).to_numpy()
    nearest = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex.to_numpy() - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    gap = np.maximum(np.maximum(mn - t, t - mx), 0)
    def m(mask):
        return float(y[mask].mean()) if mask.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    sel = (k >= 2) & (first != last)
    return m(sel & (t == first)) - m(sel & (t == last))
